output.headline: McKesson paid 25.1x for a $405M bolt-on in the target's own sub-sector, but with only one deal on record this is a lower-conviction call.
output.differentiator: Its one deal carries the highest multiple (25.1x) and the largest median deal ($405M) on the priority list, so it has shown it can pay up. The record is a single deal, though. [T:record, B:buyer]
output.why_them: Health IT bolt-on buyer; paid top multiple on its one deal

acquirer_overview.title: A strategic with one Health IT bolt-on on record
points: McKesson is a strategic buyer whose home sub-sector is Health IT, the same as the target. [B:buyer]
One deal in the file, closed in 2017, in the target's own sub-sector. No deals since 2022. [T:record, K:closed_share, K:recent]
Company profile and buyer revenue are not researched, so this view rests on deal history only. [V:synergy]

strategic_fit_thesis.title: Own sub-sector focus and margin match drive the fit
points: Share of deals in the target's sub-sector is the strongest factor. Target margin close to what it usually buys is a strong factor. [S:sector_share, S:margin_fit]
Its one deal was tagged Technology Capability, which sits on only 10% of deals in the file, and Platform Build. [M:technology_capability, M:platform_build]
The target is not bigger than any deal it has done, a slight positive. Having bought from this kind of seller is a slight negative. [S:not_bigger, S:own_fit_s]

precedent_activity.title: One precedent: a larger same-sub-sector bolt-on at a high multiple
points: Southeast Medical Informatics: $405M Bolt-on Acquisition, 2017, Health IT. It closed at 25.1x EV/EBITDA and 5.40x EV/revenue. [D:MA-2017-0106]
The deal falls in the comparable size band of $150M-$600M, where the $300M target also sits. [K:size_band]
That deal was in the Southwest. McKesson has no deal in the target's National region. [T:record, K:by_region]

valuation_context.title: Median is the anchor; McKesson's past multiple sits above the range
points: 13 comparable deals, all in the same sub-sector: 19.4x at the lower quartile, 21.4x median, 23.3x at the upper quartile. [V:comps]
Target margin of 25.0% beats the comps' median of 22.2% but is not in their top quarter, so the 50th percentile is defensible. [V:comps]
McKesson paid 25.1x on its one deal, above the upper quartile. Synergy headroom is $14M-$23M, but buyer revenue is not researched. [V:comps, V:synergy]

risk_flags.title: Thin track record
risk_flags.concern: One deal, in 2017, and none since 2022, is a narrow base for judging appetite.
risk_flags.mitigant: That deal was a same-sub-sector bolt-on larger than this target.
risk_flags.reality: The record is real but single, so intent needs a direct call. [T:record, K:recent]

risk_flags.title: Ability to pay unverified
risk_flags.concern: Buyer revenue is not researched, so capacity for a $300M deal is unconfirmed.
risk_flags.mitigant: Synergy headroom of $14M-$23M supports a bid, and the target is smaller than its past deal.
risk_flags.reality: Headroom is an estimate and does not replace balance-sheet evidence. [V:synergy, S:not_bigger]

risk_flags.title: Crowded process
risk_flags.concern: Evolent Health, Blackstone and Epic Systems each have more sub-sector deals than McKesson's one.
risk_flags.mitigant: McKesson's 25.1x is above every peer's median paid multiple.
risk_flags.reality: It ranks 9th of 10 on the priority list, with a likelihood of 3.7%. [R:rank, T:record]

conviction.rationale: Only 1 deal in the target's own sub-sector and none in the target's region, both neutral. It ranks 9th of 10 on the priority list with a likelihood of 3.7%. [C:conviction, R:rank]
